name: code-knownitem-lago
description: Known-item code retrieval over getlago/lago at 02a4bc8d (with its api and front submodules): 70 Ruby, 20 TypeScript/TSX, 15 Go and 20 Markdown targets, three queries each.

job.note: Also used as a development signal for code-ranking work (ADR-098 D4). Not blind, so never a comparison.

corpus.materialize: git archive <commit>, then each submodule's git archive at its pinned commit under its path; delete .inkentry/ before indexing

sampling.rng: Python random.seed(11); the four pools are shuffled in the order ruby, ts, go, md from one generator
sampling.source_index: chunks from an index built over a lago checkout at this commit by the inkentry build in use on 2026-09-24. That chunker emitted no chunk for a JS/TS function bound with const = arrow function, so no such function could be sampled here; code-knownitem-lago-uncovered covers them.
sampling.exclude: no name; end_line - start_line < 5; path matching (^|/)(spec|specs|test|tests|__tests__|__mocks__|e2e|cypress|fixtures?)/|[._-](spec|test)\.[jt]sx?$|_spec\.rb$|_test\.go$; path containing /vendor/; path under extra/

pools.ruby: language ruby; node_type in {method, class}; path under api/
pools.ts: language tsx or typescript; node_type in {function, method, interface, class, type_alias}; path under front/
pools.go: language go; node_type in {function, method, struct}
pools.md: language markdown; node_type section; path not matching CODE_OF_CONDUCT|CHANGELOG|LICENSE (case-insensitive)

sampling.selection: walk each shuffled pool taking at most one target per file: ruby 70, ts 20, go 15, md 20

query_authoring.method: LLM-written. For each target the model was shown the target chunk (path, name, docstring and code) and wrote one query in each of three styles.

styles.concept: plain-language description of what the code does, with no identifiers
styles.identifier: a query that contains an identifier from the target

query_authoring.caveat: The author saw the target, so wording can echo it; the identifier style names the target's own symbols by construction. Good for catching a retrieval regression, not for claiming retrieval quality or comparing against other tools.

hit_rule.chunk: hit when a ranked result in the top k has file_path equal to the target's path and a line span [start_line, end_line] that overlaps the target's (both inclusive). Rank is the 1-based position of the first such result.
hit_rule.file: hit when a ranked result in the top k has file_path equal to the target's path.
hit_rule.ranked_only: results with fused_rank null (graph or cross-project appendix members) are not scored
hit_rule.chunker_independent: the rule uses only path and line span at a pinned commit, never a chunk id, so the set survives chunker changes. A result chunk that spans the whole target region (or a large enclosing chunk) counts as a hit.

span_check: span_sha256 in targets.json is the sha256 of the target's lines start_line..end_line (1-based, inclusive) of the file at the pinned commit, as raw bytes joined by \n. The harness checks every one against the materialized corpus before indexing.

files.targets.json: tid, path, start_line, end_line, name, language, node_type, span_sha256
